stems.en:
Many times we read about Futures Trading in newspapers. What is 'Futures Trading'?
1. It is nothing but a trade between any two stock exchanges wherein it is decided to purchase the stocks of each other at a fixed price throughout the year.
2. It is an agreement between two parties to buy or sell an underlying asset in the future at a predetermined price.
3. It is an agreement between stock exchanges that they will not trade the stocks of each other under any circumstances in the future or for a given period of time.

reviewed_questions.reason: SENSEX is a weighted index of a constituent group; an index rise means an aggregate rise, not that every BSE/NSE-listed company or every constituent has risen.
reviewed_questions.previous_stem_en: A rise in SENSEX means—

previous_options_en.a: (A) a rise in prices of shares of all companies registered with Bombay Stock Exchange.
previous_options_en.b: (B) a rise in prices of shares of all companies registered with National Stock Exchange.
previous_options_en.c: (C) an overall rise in prices of shares of group of companies registered with Bombay Stock Exchange.
previous_options_en.d: (D) a rise in prices of shares of all companies belonging to a group of companies registered with Bombay Stock Exchange.

reviewed_questions.answer_text: (C) an overall rise in prices of shares of group of companies registered with Bombay Stock Exchange.

stems.en: Which base year was used for the Government of India’s Wholesale Price Index (WPI) series in 2001?
stems.hi: वर्ष 2001 में भारत सरकार की थोक मूल्य सूचकांक (WPI) श्रृंखला का आधार वर्ष कौन सा था?

reviewed_questions.notes:
The WPI series in use in 2001 had base year 1993-94. It was replaced by the 2004-05 series in September 2010.
वर्ष 2001 में उपयोग होने वाली WPI श्रृंखला का आधार वर्ष 1993-94 था। सितंबर 2010 में इसे 2004-05 आधार वाली श्रृंखला से बदल दिया गया।
reviewed_questions.previous_stem_en: The new series of Wholesale Price Index (WPI) released by the Government of India is with reference to the base prices of—

reviewed_questions.reason: NCERT gives M3 as M1 plus time deposits, while M1 includes currency and demand deposits. All three listed components belong to broad money; compare every combination.
reviewed_questions.previous_stem_en: Consider the following: 1. Currency with the public 2. Demand deposits with banks 3. Time deposits with banks Which of these are included in Broad Money (M₃) in India?

reviewed_questions.reason: SEBI’s FAQ identifies BSE IndoNext as the joint BSE/FISE alternative trading platform for regional-exchange SMEs. The January 2005 launch is corroborated by the exact UPSC 2006 fallback question; compare tourism, handicrafts and diaspora alternatives.
reviewed_questions.previous_stem_en: What is Indo Next which was launched in January 2005?

previous_options_en.a: (A) A new scheme to promote Indian tourism.
previous_options_en.b: (B) A new scheme to promote export of Indian handicrafts.
previous_options_en.c: (C) An association of the Non-Resident Indians to Organise Bharatiya Diwas every year in India.
previous_options_en.d: (D) An alternative trading platform being promoted by the Mumbai Stock Exchange and Regional Stock Exchange.

reviewed_questions.answer_text: (D) An alternative trading platform being promoted by the Mumbai Stock Exchange and Regional Stock Exchange.
